svg.title: A client who abruptly stopped long-term prednisone 2 days ago is brought to the emergency department. Blood pressure is 88/54 mm Hg , heart rate is 118/min . Labs show an elevated potassium level, a low sodium level, and a low glucose level.
svg.desc: Abrupt corticosteroid withdrawal removes the body's exogenous cortisol source and can precipitate an Addisonian crisis, which presents with hypotension, tachycardia, hyperkalemia, hyponatremia, and hypoglycemia, exactly as described. The priority is rapid IV isotonic fluid resuscitation plus IV hydrocortisone to restore volume and replace cortisol; fluid restriction and a diuretic would worsen the existing hypovolemia and hypotension. Cushing syndrome would produce the opposite picture (hypertension, hyperglycemia, hypokalemia), so it does not fit this presentation.
